name: SquadCue

hlido_opinion.headline: Unusually honest about its own limits — it calls its approval inbox a supervision workflow, not a security boundary, and points at the SECURITY.md that says so — which is rarer and more valuable than most features on this page.
hlido_opinion.body: SquadCue turns recent local Claude Code sessions into named 'employees' you can chat with, resume across restarts and supervise from your phone, with a visual canvas for orchestrating repeatable pipelines on top. The approval inbox is the substantive part: with tools allowed, a shell command or file write pauses into a queue reachable via web and Telegram, first response wins, and a timeout denies. What makes this scorecard easy to write is the vendor's own candour. The captured surface states plainly that the inbox is a supervision workflow for a trusted local setup and not a security boundary, that SECURITY.md spells out exactly what it does and does not stop, and it enumerates the deliberate bypasses by name — 'Skip approvals', the New-task 'Allow tools' box, canvas allow_tools, and the Telegram '!' prefix. Most projects in this category imply a security guarantee they cannot honour; this one pre-empts the question and names its own escape hatches. It is similarly direct elsewhere: session memory persists only as far as the session's context window, with durable cross-session memory listed as roadmap rather than shipped; discovery runs only after first-launch consent; other CLIs beyond Claude Code are a 'thin adapter layer away' rather than claimed as supported. The comparison table against n8n, Windmill, Dify and GitHub Agent HQ even concedes that n8n offers a richer canvas and tells you to use it if you want a general integration platform. The architecture is deliberately small — a FastAPI server, a one-file cockpit UI, plain JSON/JSONL and SQLite state, no Docker or build step — which is a real advantage for a local cockpit and a real limit for anything shared. Against that: it was extracted in July 2026 from one person's operation, no repository, licence, pricing or adoption signal appears on the captured page, and a Telegram-reachable approval channel over a local machine's shell deserves scrutiny the surface does not resolve.

tier_rationale: STEADY (70) because the product is coherent, the local-first architecture is well matched to its purpose, and the disclosure quality is exceptional — the vendor names its own bypasses and refuses to claim a security boundary it does not provide. It is held below the top band by the absence of licence, repository, pricing and adoption evidence, and by a very young single-operator provenance.
what_it_does_well: States explicitly that the approval inbox is a supervision workflow and not a security boundary, and points to SECURITY.md
Enumerates its own approval bypasses by name rather than leaving them for a user to discover
Describes memory honestly — persists only as far as the session context, with durable memory marked roadmap
Concedes competitors' strengths in its own comparison table and tells readers when to use n8n instead
Genuinely low-friction architecture: FastAPI server plus one-file UI, no Docker, database server or build step
State kept as plain JSON/JSONL and SQLite files, described as greppable — inspectable and portable
Approval routing across web and Telegram with first-response-wins and timeout-equals-deny is a sensible default
Session rescue after reboot addresses a real, unglamorous failure in day-to-day agent operation
what_it_fails_at: No repository, licence, pricing or adoption signal on the captured surface
Extracted in July 2026 from a single-person operation — no continuity, contributor or maintenance evidence
Approval gate is explicitly not a security control, so it cannot be relied on where one is needed
Claude Code is the only first-class engine; other CLIs are described as an adapter layer away, not supported today
A Telegram-reachable approval channel controlling a local machine's shell introduces a trust surface the page does not resolve
Local-only control plane rules out team or multi-operator use by design
best_for: Solo operators running several Claude Code sessions who want a cockpit with names, queues and approvals
People who want to supervise long-running local agents from a phone rather than a terminal
Users who value inspectable local state and a zero-infrastructure install over hosted convenience
not_recommended_for: Teams needing shared, multi-user orchestration — the control plane is deliberately local
Anyone who needs the approval gate to function as an actual security boundary
Organisations requiring licence clarity, support or continuity guarantees
Users of AI CLIs other than Claude Code today
red_flags: The approval inbox is explicitly not a security boundary and several documented bypasses exist by design — do not deploy it where a real control is required. Credit to the vendor for saying so; the caution stands regardless.
No licence or repository is visible on the captured surface for software that reads local sessions and gates shell execution — establish both before installing.

compared_to.verdict_diff: Both put a human in front of risky agent actions. phinq is a focused, MIT-licensed approval layer that presents itself as a control; SquadCue wraps approvals inside a broader session-management cockpit and explicitly declines to call them a security boundary. phinq for the gate, SquadCue for the cockpit.

Both take a small-tools, local-first stance rather than an everything-platform one. Axe composes single-purpose agents in the Unix tradition; SquadCue supervises full interactive CLI sessions as long-lived contacts. Different granularity, similar philosophy.

evidence_urls.claim: Approval inbox pauses shell commands and file writes via web and Telegram, first response wins, timeout denies
Vendor states the inbox is a supervision workflow and not a security boundary
Local-first: FastAPI server and one-file UI, state in JSON/JSONL and SQLite, no Docker or build step
Claude Code sessions become resumable named contacts with persistent session memory
Support for AI CLIs other than Claude Code and Codex

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Not an agent an external system integrates with — it is a control plane for locally-running AI CLI sessions. Integrates downward into Claude Code via a PreToolUse hook and session resume, and outward to Telegram for approvals. Runs entirely on the operator's machine, so it is not testable from a public surface.

marking_signal.reason: SquadCue supervises and orchestrates local AI CLI sessions; it does not itself generate synthetic media or published text, so Article-50 output-marking obligations do not attach.

summary: Unusually honest about its own limits — it calls its approval inbox a supervision workflow, not a security boundary, and points at the SECURITY.md that says so — which is rarer and more valuable than most features on this page.
